deals.name: 250 NW 10th Street — Waukee, IA
deals.nextAction:
[2026-07-25 PM — zoning re-verification, corrects the earlier same-day note] ZONING FINDING IS MORE SERIOUS THAN FIRST REPORTED — possible use-legality problem, not just a boundary-precision question. Do not advance to LOI until resolved.

What changed from the morning note: (1) precise edge distance computed from the actual C-1 zoning polygon vertices (not a 4-point spot-check) — the address point sits only ~4.7m (~15 FEET) from the parcel's eastern zoning-district boundary, not ~65m as first estimated. (2) Stepped queries at 5m/15m/50m east of that exact edge show the ADJACENT zone is R-2 ONE AND TWO-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL, not M-1A — M-1A Limited Industrial only begins somewhere between 15-50m further east, beyond the residential strip. Source: City of Waukee zoning GIS (services2.arcgis.com/PsFb8xDKjNyDsxki/.../Zoning/FeatureServer/0), queried and geometrically verified 2026-07-25.

THE MATERIAL ISSUE: pulled the actual C-1 (§169.14) and C-1A (§169.15, which C-1 incorporates by reference) ordinance text directly from the City of Waukee's own published PDFs (waukee.org/DocumentCenter, Ordinance 2987, verified 2026-07-25). C-1's full permitted-use list is retail, professional office, hospitals, animal hospital, bowling alley, brew pub, clubs/lodges, funeral homes, grocery, appliance sales/repair, auto sales/service, hotels, and "Interior Self Storage" — plus everything in C-1A (medical/professional offices, personal services, neighborhood retail, capped at 50,000 SF/building). NOWHERE in either list is warehouse, distribution, industrial, manufacturing, or general contractor/outdoor storage a permitted use. If the deal's contemplated use is a 108,800 SF industrial/warehouse building — which is what this pipeline entry assumes — that use does not appear to be permitted under the zoning that actually governs this address today.

Open questions the formal municipal zoning letter (already mandatory pre-LOI) must resolve, now with higher stakes: (a) is the existing/intended industrial use a legal NONCONFORMING use predating a rezone to C-1 — if so get the nonconforming-use determination in writing, since nonconforming rights can be lost on a change of use/ownership or if vacant too long; (b) was the parcel actually rezoned to something else (M-1A/M-1) that this GIS layer hasn't caught up to — possible but unverified; (c) if neither (a) nor (b), this deal needs a rezone or use variance before any industrial tenancy is lawful, which is a materially different risk/timeline than a clean by-right industrial parcel.

VERDICT IMPACT: escalate from "resolve boundary + obtain zoning letter" to "the zoning letter must affirmatively address use-legality, not just confirm the district." Do not rely on the GIS screen alone for this deal — a call to Waukee planning/zoning before any further underwriting time is spent would be the efficient next step. Flood determination (Zone X, no SFHA) stands from the earlier note and is unaffected by this correction. Remaining open items unchanged: replacement-cost verification, reassessed-tax confirmation.
